A01:2025.name: Broken Access Control
A01:2025.description: Restrictions on authenticated users are not properly enforced. Attackers exploit these flaws to access unauthorized functionality and data, including viewing others' records, elevating privileges, or acting as other users.

A02:2025.name: Security Misconfiguration
A02:2025.description: Missing appropriate security hardening across the application stack. Unnecessary features are enabled, default accounts remain unchanged, or overly permissive settings expose attack surface.

A03:2025.name: Software Supply Chain Failures
A03:2025.description: NEW in 2025. Risks introduced through third-party components, open-source libraries, build pipelines, and software delivery processes. Includes compromised packages, typosquatting, and CI/CD pipeline tampering.

A04:2025.name: Cryptographic Failures
A04:2025.description: Failures related to cryptography that lead to sensitive data exposure or system compromise. Includes weak algorithms, poor key management, and cleartext transmission of sensitive data.
examples: use of ECB mode or CBC without integrity

A05:2025.name: Injection
A05:2025.description: User-supplied data is not validated, filtered, or sanitized. The interpreter executes hostile commands or queries, leading to data theft, corruption, or remote code execution.

A06:2025.name: Insecure Design
A06:2025.description: Missing or ineffective security controls arising from design and architecture flaws. Cannot be fixed by a correct implementation alone — the design must be changed.
examples: no separation of duties in sensitive operations

A07:2025.name: Authentication Failures
A07:2025.description: Authentication and session management flaws allow attackers to compromise passwords, keys, or session tokens, or exploit implementation weaknesses to assume users' identities.
examples: credentials exposed in URLs or logs

A08:2025.name: Software or Data Integrity Failures
A08:2025.description: Code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations. Includes insecure deserialization, untrusted plugin or update mechanisms, and reliance on unsigned data.
examples: deserialization of YAML/XML without schema validation

A09:2025.name: Security Logging and Alerting Failures
A09:2025.description: Insufficient logging, detection, and response capabilities allow attackers to maintain persistence, pivot to more systems, and exfiltrate or destroy data without timely detection.
examples: logs stored only locally without integrity protection
no audit trail for sensitive operations

A10:2025.name: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
A10:2025.description: NEW in 2025. Applications that fail to properly handle errors, exceptions, or unexpected states expose internal details, enter inconsistent states, or can be crashed by attackers — enabling information disclosure, denial of service, or logic bypass.
examples: null pointer dereference without graceful handling
uncaught async errors crashing the server
